MetLife Submission of Claims  Policy  
 
 
 
 
Submission of Claims : 
 
MetLife offers several ways to submit claims that can help you save time and energy, and may 
help control overhead costs.  
 
• Electronic Claims  
▪ Through your Practice Management System (PMS)  
▪ Online via www.MetDental.com   
▪ Web-based submission via clearinghouse  
 
• Telephone via 1 -877-MET-DDS9 (638 -3379)   
 
• By fax vis 1 -859-389-6505  
 
• Mail claims to:   
MetLife Dental Claims  
P.O. Box 9812 82 
El Paso, TX 79998 -1282  
 
Submit your normal charges when sending claims to MetLife.  
 
Our claims payment system will adjust the fees so that the Explanation of Benefits shows both 
the submitted charge and the allowable charge. By submitting normal charge s, you help MetLife 
maintain accurate data for reasonable and customary charges and your usual charge on our 
claim payment system. When your usual charge for a procedure is lower than the plan 
allowance, your usual charge will become the maximum amount you  may bill a participant.  
 
Although participants may not always inform your office of their participation in the program, 
MetLife’s claim payment system automatically recognizes both the dentist’s and the patient’s 
participation and determines applicable pl an allowances when the claim is processed.  
 
MetLife dental consultants may review codes submitted and provide an alternative service to a 
submitted code when the alternative service more closely resembles the service rendered. 
Participating dentists agree to the negotiated fee of the service that more closely resembles the 
service rendered.

MetLife Utilization Review  Policy  
 
 
 
 
Utilization Review:  
 
Provider Utilization Profile (PUP) evaluation is a mandatory component of the selection and 
retention process. The Provider Utilization Profile System is a statistically based utilization 
review system designed to identify dentists’ treatment patterns. Dentists whose practice 
patterns fall outside PUP guidelines or who fail to comply with PUP or program administrative 
procedures may not be acceptable for initial or continued participation.  
 
MetLife or its designated credentialing vendor performs Provider Utilization Profiling on all 
applicants from a national database maintained by the designated credentialing vendor. T his 
database contains individual dental procedure utilization rates, defined as norms, and individual 
provider utilization profiles. These norms are compared to the individual Provider’s Utilization 
Profile to determine which dentists are at a variance wit h the norm. A provider is determined to 
be at a variance with a norm when the provider performs at least one of the measured 
procedures at a rate that exceeds 85% of the other dentists in the area. If a profile meets 
MetLife guidelines, the provider will b e considered for participation; otherwise, he/she may be 
counseled regarding changes that would allow him/her to be reconsidered.  
 
A provider who does not demonstrate an acceptable Provider Utilization Profile may be selected 
for participation at the discr etion of MetLife’s National Dental Director. This will be a provisional 
acceptance with MetLife Claim Review (MCR) applied for at least six months.
